items.title: Ukraine defence minister resigns as part of Zelensky's cabinet reshuffle
items.description: Ukraine's Defence Minister Mykhailo Fedorov announced his resignation on Wednesday as part of President Volodymyr Zelensky's cabinet reshuffle, stepping down after overseeing a rapid expansion of drone warfare capabilities and military reforms during Russia's full-scale invasion.

items.title: Sen. Shaheen discusses new Russia sanctions bill
items.description: A conversation with Jeanne Shaheen, Democratic Senator from New Hampshire, about a bipartisan bill she put together with the late Senator Lindsey Graham that slaps new sanctions on Russia.

items.title: Russia Fires 6,001 Drones, 170 Bombs as Ukraine Repels 235 Clashes
items.description: The Armed Forces of Ukraine repelled 235 clashes across the front line on Wednesday, July 15, with the heaviest fighting near Pokrovsk and Kostiantynivka. Russian forces used 170 guided bombs and 6,001 kamikaze drones during the assault.

items.title: Palestinians in Gaza: Stuck between Hamas and Israel
items.description: Hamas is planning to transfer control of Gaza's civilian administration to Palestinian technocrats as part of the fragile US ceasefire. How is that affecting the daily lives of people living in Gaza?

items.title: After Double Amputation, Ukrainian Vet Says 'Thirst For Independence' Led The Way To Recovery

items.title: Israeli strike on police post in north Gaza kills seven, officials say
items.description: A senior officer in the Hamas-run police force was among those killed in the strike, which Israel's military says targeted "terrorists".

items.title: Winter was harsh, but resilient Odesa making summer a season of hope
items.description: Odesa, home to a Ukrainian seaport that is a critical link in the global food security chain, endured its worst winter of Russian attacks since the war began, then prepared for a vibrant summer with a determination not just to survive but to build a better future.
